==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
First use appears c. 1542, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} {{m|la|prosecutor}}, from {{m|la|prōsequor}} (English {{m|en|prosecute}}).<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> {{surf|en|prosecute|-or}}.

===Pronunciation===
*{{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑ.səˌkjuːˌtəɹ/|a=US}}
*{{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-prosecutor.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Noun===
{{wp}}
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q600751}}A [[prosecuting attorney]].
#: {{ux|en|Annie Jay was the Wisconsin government '''prosecutor''' in the trial of a man for forging his client's signature.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=February 22, 2008|title=Now a Reminder From Mr. Cunningham|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/22/opinion/22fri4.html
|passage=It sat by mutely while Jack Abramoff, the superlobbyist, spun schemes that eroded public trust, until '''prosecutors''' had to move in.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240922213119/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/22/opinion/22fri4.html|archivedate=22 September 2024}}
# {{lb|en|law}} A [[person]], as a [[complainant]], [[victim]], or [[chief]] [[witness]], who [[institute]]s [[prosecution]] in a [[criminal]] [[proceeding]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''prosecutor''' got the witness to admit he was lying.}}
